summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of anxiety and gastroparesis was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis and gastroenteritis, likely triggered by insulin nonadherence during a viral illness that also affected her son. She presented with vomiting, diarrhea, and hyperglycemia, and was treated with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin as her metabolic panel stabilized. Coffee-ground emesis was attributed to esophagitis or a Mallory-Weiss tear from repeated vomiting, and she was maintained on pantoprazole. Anxiety was managed with scheduled lorazepam, and metoclopramide was started for nausea. Her kidney function, affected by stage I diabetic nephropathy, improved with hydration. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue insulin, metoclopramide, and lorazepam, and to follow up with her primary care provider and psychiatrist.
